summary: State-owned steel fire tower on Croydon Peak inside the private Corbin Park; rebuilt after the 1938 hurricane, recabbed in 2009, not open to the public.

facts.design: two-tier steel-frame tower with a square hip-roof wood-frame cab

staffing.status: one of 15 active fire towers the state owns and runs; no staffing detail for this tower in the sources

access.note: Inside Corbin Park, a private game preserve. Not open to the public. The state uses one acre on the summit under a 1950 lease from the Blue Mountain Forest Association.

visit.trail_note: Inside a private preserve. Wikipedia says the mountain is not accessible to hikers, and the tower is not open to the public.

events.note: Corbin Park began a fire protection program
A.L. Lurvey built a watchman's cabin on the peak
Forestry commissioner's report mentions a station on the mountain kept by the Draper Company and the Blue Mountain Park Association
Blue Mountain Forest Association installed a fire tower with the support of the Draper Company (first-station year differs from the 1909 report; see resolved_conflicts)
Tower upgraded to a 17-foot steel frame with a 10-by-10-foot cab
Lookout destroyed in the Great New England Hurricane, September 21, 1938 (Forest Lookouts date)
Steel replacement built as a fire tower; Historic Structures gives its height as 24 feet in one section and 34 feet in another
Blue Mountain Forest Association leased one acre on the summit to the state for one dollar (lease dated March 13, 1950)
Taken out of service to finance a five-year trial of fire detection by air patrol
Reopened after the air patrol program was not continued
Most recent renewal of the state's agreement with the Blue Mountain Forest Association
Cab substantially rebuilt, with materials helicoptered onto the summit; monitoring equipment not installed in the new cab

corrections.why: The 2009 chapter report says the state replaced the tower cab, not the tower. Historic Structures dates the steel tower itself to 1938.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Historic Structures gives the 1938 replacement as 24 feet in its history section and as 34 feet tall in its description section. The story reports both figures and does not pick one. No height is set in the facts.

Historic Structures puts the Draper Company-backed tower in 1910. A 1909 forestry commissioner's report, quoted by Forest Lookouts, already describes a station on the mountain kept by the Draper Company and the park association. The story gives both years.

Sources use Croydon Peak (FFLA list, Historic Structures) and Croydon Mountain (Forest Lookouts, and the state lease wording quoted by Historic Structures). They appear to describe the same summit and tower; the story says so.

sources.title: Croydon Peak Fire Tower, Newport New Hampshire

notes_for_editor: The main history comes from Historic Structures, which reproduces a detailed description of the tower and its history. It is a secondary source and its own citations are not visible to us, so treat its dates as strong but not verified against the state record. The Forest Lookouts page has only three dated lines. The 2009 record event should be 'modified' (cab), not 'replaced' (tower); see corrections. Height is unresolved (24 ft vs 34 ft) and is left out of facts. Access: the tower is inside a private preserve and the sources say it is closed to the public, so the record should not invite climbing. Leads: the NH Fire Tower Quest Program PDF from NH Forests & Lands, cited by the Corbin Park Wikipedia article (not fetched; the state site returned 403 for the related history PDF); and the Blue Mountain Forest Association for lease and access terms.
